title: AMD Unveils Local Coding Platform Instinct Coder 355: One Machine Packs in 98% of Frontier Models

content_html:
AMD is pulling large models out of the cloud and back into the data center—and this time, it is going after the enterprise developer business. On November 9 local time, AMD teamed up with Spectro Cloud to launch Instinct Coder 355, an enterprise-grade AI coding assistant platform that can run GLM-5.3 inference locally and is said to come close to 98% of the performance of frontier models.

Eight cards power one coding server

The system’s real muscle is in its hardware: at its core are 8 AMD Instinct MI355X accelerators, paired with 2 64-core EPYC 9575F "Zen 5" processors, plus 3TB of DDR5-6400 memory and a total of 63.36TB of solid-state storage. Dell and Supermicro offer fully configured systems with different specifications, so enterprises can choose a setup that fits their data center practices. A single node can serve up to 85 developers, with 50 able to code online at the same time—effectively packing a small team’s compute needs into one chassis.

No cloud by default, data stays local

What really appeals to enterprises is the "stay in-house" setup. Spectro Cloud provides PaletteAI Inference Launchpad management software for the system, which uses local compute rather than cloud APIs by default, so sensitive code and data do not have to be sent outside. Under the dual pressure of cost and compliance, moving inference back to in-house data centers is becoming a new direction that major players are betting on—and with this move, AMD clearly wants a share of the pie currently held by Nvidia and the various cloud providers.
